Your Eyes and Ears

Oxford Read and Discover · Level 2 · Your Body · Pages 10–11

🔒 New Words 1 · Listen & Fill 2 · Write 3 · Present 4 · Mind Map

★ New Words

🔒 This part is for the teacher.

Teach these words before the listening task. Press 🔊 to hear the word (American English). Show the picture, read the meaning, then read the example.

world

noun

All the places and people on Earth.

“Your eyes help you to see the world.”

around

preposition

On every side of something.

“You see the world around you.”

blink

verb

To close and open your eyes very fast.

“When your eyes blink, they wash dirt out.”

night

noun

The dark time when you sleep.

“At night your eyes close.”

listen

verb

To use your ears to hear something.

“Your ears help you to listen to music.”

street

noun

A road in a town with houses and cars.

“Listen for cars in the street.”

hear

verb

To get sounds with your ears.

“Your ears can hear things when you sleep.”

sunny

adjective

When the sun is shining.

“On sunny days, wear sunglasses.”

sunglasses

noun

Dark glasses that protect your eyes from the sun.

“Wear sunglasses to protect your eyes.”

loud

adjective

Making a very big sound.

“Don’t listen to very loud music.”

2 Write a Summary

Write about your eyes and ears in your own words. Write 15 words or more. Then you can see my example.

💡 Answer these questions

  1. What do your eyes help you do?
  2. What is blinking?
  3. What does blinking do?
  4. What do your ears help you do?
  5. How can you protect your eyes?
  6. How can you protect your ears?

✏️ Start like this

  • My eyes help me to …
  • Blinking is when …
  • When my eyes blink, …
  • My ears help me to …
  • On sunny days, I …
  • I don’t listen to …
0 / 15 words

⭐ Example Summary

My eyes help me to see the world around me. They open and close many times every day. This is called blinking. Blinking washes dirt out of my eyes. My ears help me to listen to music and to listen for cars in the street. On sunny days, I wear sunglasses to protect my eyes. I don’t listen to very loud music because it’s bad for my ears.

3 Presentation Script

Read the script. Practise it. Then present to your class!

Hello!Start

Good morning, everyone! My name is ________. Today I want to talk about my eyes and my ears.

Let’s start with a game. Close your eyes… now open your eyes!

👉 Close and open your eyes with the class.
Part 1Eyes

Our eyes help us to see the world around us.

👉 Point to your eyes, then look around the room.
Part 2Blinking

Our eyes open and close many times every day. This is called blinking.

When our eyes blink, they wash dirt out of our eyes. At night our eyes close so we can sleep.

Fun fact: Eyes blink about 15 times every minute!

👉 Show the two pictures: eyes closed, eyes open.
Part 3Ears

Our ears help us to listen to music. They help us to listen for cars in the street.

Our ears can hear things when we sleep, too!

👉 Put your hand behind your ear. Say “Listen!”
Part 4Protect eyes

How can we protect our eyes? On sunny days, we wear sunglasses.

👉 Show the picture. Pretend to put on sunglasses.
Part 5Protect ears

How can we protect our ears? Don’t listen to very loud music – it’s bad for our ears!

Question for you: Do you wear sunglasses? (Wait for answers.)

👉 Cover your ears. Then ask the class.
The EndFinish

Remember: our eyes see and our ears hear. Let’s protect them!

Thank you for listening! Do you have any questions?

👉 Smile and say “Thank you!”

🌟 Presentation Tips

  • Speak slowly and loudly.
  • Look at your friends, not only at the paper.
  • Point to the pictures when you talk.
  • Smile! 😊
